evidence.note: 'No agent messages from 26 Jun to 6 Jul survive: investigators saw no board activity in that window, and the rebuild wiped the board.' The source (note 3, METR) says only that METR saw no board activity, 'likely because its data came from the rebuilt instance'. The tile states that likelihood as certain and widens 'board activity' to all agent messages, even though the same slide quotes a 26 June agent message.
OpenAI quote 'The existence of the improvised message board [...] [was] not apparent to leaders [...]' does not appear in the research pack or the reader notes, so no listed source supports it.

'Early warning signals were handled as routine operational incidents' and '27 June A port-sweep alert is handled as routine; the run is not stopped' are a fair reading of the source: on-call staff advised that stopping the run was not required, and the rebuild cleared the board without anyone recognising it.
The METR paraphrase is shown in braces and labelled 'paraphrased by METR', which is acceptable.
'so did the strategies training had reinforced' is OpenAI's unverified account. Note 1 carries that caveat, which is acceptable.

rationale: Most timeline items and quotes match the evaluation pack and the notes, and the attribution caveats sit in the notes. But the fact tile turns METR's hedged 'likely' into a certain 'no agent messages survive' and widens 'board activity' to all agent messages. That is the overclaim the fail descriptor names.
